title: Training Note — Recurring Fees in a Catch-Up Amount
content:
The share of a late period's still-unpaid recurring fees that an Apartment Home Lease catch-up amount carries follows the autopay record: a lease with ten or more ACH autopay lease payments dated in the last 12 months carries none of them, because they ride on the next draft; a lease with six to nine carries half (0.5) of them, rounded half up to the cent; any other lease carries all of them.

## Questions answered

**What counts toward the autopay record?** Lease payments on the Apartment Home Lease ledger made by ACH autopay and dated in the last 12 months — after the same day of the month twelve months before the handling date. Payments by any other instrument do not count.

**Which recurring fees are meant?** The period's recurring fees (its lease fee lines) that remain unpaid once the period's payments have been applied.

**What does "half, rounded half up" give on an odd-cent figure?** Half of $94.01 is $47.005, which rounds half up to $47.01.

## Record table

| ACH autopay lease payments in the last 12 months | Share of still-unpaid recurring fees carried |
|---|---|
| 10 or more | none |
| 6 to 9 | half, rounded half up to the cent |
| 5 or fewer | all |

**Boundaries.** 9 drafts carry half; 10 carry none. 5 drafts carry all; 6 carry half.

*Hypothetical:* $94.00 of recurring fees still unpaid — with 12 drafts in the window the amount carries $0.00; with 7 drafts, $47.00; with 3 drafts, $94.00.
